small_guidance:
- The ConvTranspose2d is doing essentially all the work (output is N×128×256×256 ≈ 134M elements per batch); tuning the tiny min/sum/gelu tails further cannot meaningfully improve fast_p. If staying small, at least fuse the min-reduce and sum-along-H into a single kernel (one program per (N, w) that loops over H, and inside reduces over C) to eliminate the intermediate (N,1,H,W) tensor write/read.
- For that fused tail kernel, use BLOCK_W=128, num_warps=8, num_stages=2, and load a (BLOCK_C, BLOCK_W) tile per H-step with BLOCK_C=128 (matches out_channels exactly, no masking).
- Make sure conv_transpose output is consumed in channels-last so the C-min reduction is contiguous; currently the min kernel strides by H*W across the reduction axis which is the slowest possible layout.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose2d` with a custom scatter-add Triton kernel (input × weight outer product scattered into the (N, OC, H_out, W_out) grid with stride=2, padding=1, output_padding=1). This is where >95% of runtime lives; the current implementation still calls torch's ConvTranspose2d so fast_p is capped at ~baseline/conv_time.
- Fuse the entire tail (min over C, sum over H, GELU, bias-add) directly into the conv-transpose epilogue: have each program accumulate its OC tile's contribution to an output column, then after the conv loop reduce across C to get min, across H to get sum, apply GELU and bias, and store only the final (N,1,1,W_out) tensor. The full intermediate (N,128,256,256) never needs to be materialized — but the multiply-accumulate count of the conv must remain the full reference count (iterate over all kh,kw,IC for every (n,oc,h_out,w_out)).
- Alternative cleaner split: (1) gemm-style conv-transpose kernel writing the full (N,OC,H,W) output (channels-last), then (2) a single fused min-sum-gelu-bias kernel over (N,W) that loops H and reduces C inline. This keeps the conv kernel reusable and still removes one full pass over the giant tensor.
